title: Installing Cloud Code
content:
To install Cloud Code, use the following commands:
- For macOS, Linux, or WSL: Use curl command to install it in one go.
- For Homebrew users: Use brew install to install, but note it lacks auto-update capabilities.
- For Windows: Use Invoke-RestMethod in PowerShell or curl command in CMD. A winget command is also available, but it won't auto-update.

After installation, go to your project directory and run Cloud. You will be prompted to choose your color theme and sign in with your Cloud account (Pro, Max, or Enterprise) or use an API key. If your organization has a specific account, you can use that instead.
raw_text: Cloud Code is simple to install whether you want to use it in your terminal, the web, or your IDE. If you're on macOS, Linux, or WSL, use this curl command to install it in one go. If you prefer to use Homebrew, you can also use brew install to install it, but note that this doesn't have auto-update capabilities. For Windows, there's also a couple ways. In PowerShell, use the Invoke-RestMethod command. If you're on CMD, you can also use this curl command. We also have a winget command as well if you prefer, but just like Homebrew, it won't auto-update. Now, go to your project directory and run Cloud. You will go through some initial instructions like choosing your color theme and signing in with your Cloud account, which could be the Pro, Max, or Enterprise. Or you can use an API key.
